topic.seo_description: Explore fisetin research for cancer treatment. Learn about this senolytic flavonoid's potential, clinical trials, and latest scientific findings.
topic.seo_intro:
Fisetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid compound found in various fruits and vegetables that has attracted significant attention from cancer researchers in recent years. As a senolytic agent—a substance that selectively eliminates senescent cells—fisetin represents a novel approach to cancer treatment that differs from traditional chemotherapy. Senescent cells are aging cells that can accumulate in tumors and contribute to cancer progression, chemotherapy resistance, and tumor microenvironment changes that support cancer growth. By targeting and removing these problematic cells, fisetin may help reduce tumor burden and improve treatment outcomes.

The current state of fisetin research for cancer is still largely in preclinical and early clinical stages. Laboratory studies have demonstrated promising anti-cancer properties, including the ability to trigger apoptosis (programmed cell death) in cancer cells and inhibit tumor growth in animal models. Researchers are particularly interested in fisetin's potential to work synergistically with existing cancer therapies and its favorable safety profile as a naturally-derived compound. However, more clinical trials are needed to establish its efficacy and optimal dosing in human cancer patients.

This page compiles the latest peer-reviewed research on fisetin and cancer to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers stay informed about emerging evidence. While the findings are encouraging, it's important to note that fisetin should not replace conventional cancer treatments without medical consultation. The articles and studies featured below represent the most current scientific investigations into fisetin's role in cancer research and treatment.

articles.title: Fisetin Promotes Autophagy in Osteosarcoma by Activating the ROS/FOXO3 Axis via Oxidative Stress.
articles.hook: Fisetin triggers autophagy in osteosarcoma cells via ROS/FOXO3 pathway
articles.summary: Fisetin, a plant compound, slows osteosarcoma growth by triggering a cellular cleanup process that leads to cancer cell death.

articles.title: Fisetin promotes liver regeneration by inducing β-catenin-mediated inhibition of p53 and suppression of TGF-β.
articles.summary: Fisetin, a natural antioxidant, accelerates liver regeneration after surgery by activating β-catenin and blocking senescence and growth-inhibiting pathways.

articles.title: pH-responsive Folate-PEG modified ZIF-8 Nanoparticles deliver fisetin to Aquaporin-3 for cervical cancer therapy.
articles.summary: Researchers developed targeted nanoparticles delivering fisetin to cervical cancer cells by blocking a protein that disrupts tumor metabolism and growth.

articles.title: Synergistic anticancer effects of tamoxifen in combination with fisetin and chrysin on breast cancer cells: insights into viability, migration, and apoptosis.
articles.summary: Combining tamoxifen with fisetin and chrysin significantly enhanced breast cancer cell death and reduced cancer cell migration and survival.

articles.title: Overcoming Intrinsic and Acquired Temozolomide Resistance in Glioblastoma: Fisetin as a Potential Strategy to Enhance Sensitivity via ZEB1 Modulation.

articles.summary: Fisetin, a natural compound, can help overcome temozolomide resistance in glioblastoma by modulating ZEB1 and potentially improving treatment effectiveness.
